title: C vs C++: what changed
learningGoals: name four differences between C and C++
print with cout instead of printf
use std:: in front of library names

youtube.title: C vs C++: What Changed? | C++ Programming EP 03
youtube.description: In this episode you will name four differences between C and C++, print with cout instead of printf and use std:: in front of library names, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 C vs C++: what changed · 0:50 The C way · 1:30 C and C++ side by side · 2:06 Second program · 3:06 Recap · 3:38 Bug of the Day · 4:26 Challenge · 4:46 Next episode

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we compare C and C plus plus. You will see what stayed the same, and what is new.

scenes.onScreen: "C vs C++: what changed": numbered lines (1. C++ grew out of C; 2. C++ adds classes and a bigger library; 3. Most C code still works in C++) and an analogy card: a bicycle and a motorbike: both carry you, but one has more features
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: C plus plus grew out of the C language. Most C code still works in C plus plus. But C plus plus adds many features. It has classes, a bigger library, and safer ways to handle memory. Think of a bicycle and a motorbike. Both carry you to school. The motorbike has more parts, so you must learn more.
points: C++ adds classes and a bigger library
Most C code still works in C++

analogy.title: C vs C++: what changed
analogy.body: A bicycle and a motorbike: both carry you, but one has more features

scenes.onScreen: cstyle.cpp: printf prints text, as in C
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 1] The header cstdio gives us printf, the C way to print. [HL 4] Printf works in C plus plus too. The backslash n at the end starts a new line. Notice the prefix std colon colon. C plus plus keeps its library names inside the std namespace.

scenes.onScreen: a table: feature, C way, C++ way
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: Here are five differences. For printing, C uses printf, and C plus plus uses cout. For reading, C uses scanf, and C plus plus uses cin. For text, C uses char arrays, and C plus plus has std string. For memory, C plus plus gives you smart pointers. For grouping data, C plus plus has classes. We will learn each one.

diagram.caption: a table: feature, C way, C++ way

scenes.onScreen: cppstyle.cpp: cout prints text, as in C++
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 4] Now the C plus plus way. The cout tool takes the text with the insertion operator, which looks like two arrows. The endl word ends the line. [HL 5] The program returns zero, as before. Both styles give the same result on the screen.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as cppstyle dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. Both programs print one hello line. C plus plus lets you choose either style.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. C plus plus grew out of C. Two. Printf is the C way, and cout is the C plus plus way. Three. Library names live in the std namespace. Four. C plus plus adds classes, strings and smart pointers. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: C plus plus grew out of C.
Printf is the C way, and cout is the C plus plus way.
Library names live in the std namespace.
C plus plus adds classes, strings and smart pointers.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: Forgetting std
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Here we write cout without std in front. The compiler says cout was not declared in this scope. It also suggests std colon colon cout. Library names live in the std namespace. Add the prefix, and the error goes away.

scenes.onScreen: Why did C plus plus not invite C to the party? C said, I will be there, but only as a subset.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why did C plus plus not invite C to the party? C said, I will be there, but only as a subset.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: print with printf and cout in one program

scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write one program that prints one line with printf and one line with cout. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.onScreen: Next: EP 04 · Anatomy of a C++ program

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

cppstyle.cpp: In function 'int main()':
cppstyle.cpp:4:5: error: 'cout' was not declared in this scope; did you mean 'std::cout'?
    4 |     cout << "Hello from C++ style" << std::endl;
      |     ^~~~
      |     std::cout
bug.why: Library names such as cout live in the std namespace. Write std colon colon in front, or use a using line, which we learn soon.

pun: "Why did C plus plus not invite C to the party? C said, I will be there, but only as a subset."
challenge: Write one program that prints one line with printf and one line with cout.
challengeAnswer: Include both cstdio and iostream. Call std printf with a backslash n, then use std cout with endl.
